facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
who worked as a butcher and occasional hunter and had contact with hares and rabbits
lesions on left hand evolving over 3 days
vesiculobullous lesions appeared on the dorsal aspect of his left hand and extended into the web space between the first and second fingers
the lesion extended to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area on which pustules appeared
No fever or other systemic symptoms were present
Hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of left hand extending to web space between first and second fingers
Surface erosion with pustular lesions on palm and ventral aspect of thumb
Fungal culture was negative
bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative
Initially hemorrhagic bullous lesions appeared

concepts.why: The patient has lesions on the left hand with hemorrhagic bullous lesions and pustules, and bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans.
The patient has a history of contact with hares and rabbits, and presented with lesions on the left hand, which could be consistent with cutaneous tularemia.
The patient has a history of contact with animals, and presented with lesions on the left hand, which could be consistent with erysipeloid.
The patient has lesions on the left hand with hemorrhagic bullous lesions and pustules, and bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans, which could be consistent with cellulitis.

The negative fungal culture and negative polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, along with the patient's contact with hares and rabbits, suggest tularemia as a possible diagnosis.

rationales.F02: Contact with hares and rabbits increases the likelihood of zoonotic infections such as tularemia and erysipeloid.
rationales.F10: The presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture strongly supports a staphylococcal skin infection.
rationales.F11: The negative PCR result for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae makes erysipeloid less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans, which directly supports Staphylococcal skin infection, while contact with animals and occupation suggest but do not strongly confirm Erysipeloid
